about: FoodBlock 1.7: every closed list and grammar in the spec (core.md, modules/ and profiles/), for code to load. Where the spec states a list, it matches this file exactly. Year zero is 1.6: no older shape is read, and 1.7 adds to it except the few deletions CHANGELOG.md lists.
type_about: Any other type name matching grammar.type_name is open: stored and passed on, no authority.

needs.about: order: refs that order blocks by cause (a block's causal past also holds every block it names by counted_to). needs: the blocks a block rests on, by type: its author's genesis, its prev, the grant (or rule) it acts under, and for a closed type the schema it names, whose fields and roles it may carry. A block waits until all it needs are held, and is judged once, on them alone (core.md, section 8); a fold reads the largest part of its input in which every block is valid on what it rests on and has all it needs.

refs.about: Shared ref keys are these lists plus the verbs and the causal keys. refs.of names the kind an instance belongs to; state.kind is a label.

refs_single_about: These links hold exactly one id; an array there is `grammar` (core.md, section 1): an answer answers one block, a stop or a new version updates one, a block speaks as one circle, acts under one grant, and a grant passes on one parent. A promise's sides (from, to) are one id each too (promises.md, Sides: `shape`).
statuses_about: A counter-offer is an answer (a promise with refs.answers) whose state carries new terms and no status; it is the one answer without a status.

stop.occurrences: { occurrences: [start times, or the hashes of the blocks that started them] }: named occurrences of a standing promise

circle.removal_rule: Each circle states its removal rule at founding, state.removal { needed: N } on the circle actor; with none stated, no one who holds admit or remove is removed (folds.md, Counts). needed 1: any holder of remove alone removes anyone, as in a chat group's admins. Removing a holder of admit or remove takes at least `needed` different holders of remove, the remover among them, each stopping that same member grant. The member removed never counts among them.
circle.roles_shape: state.roles: [{ name, powers }]; the founding block is the founder's first member grant, giving the first role; powers are from `powers` and from profile powers, and no one gives a power they do not hold
circle.needed_rule: state.needed: { sign: N } on the circle actor: a block signed as the circle speaks for it once N different holders of sign have signed it, its author and holders who `confirms` it, each in their own block's fold and within the cuts of their ended grants. With none, one holder's signature, as for any block. Admitting and removing keep their own rules (removal).

genesis.private_about: A genesis may carry any audience (decision H10): public, or a sorted list of commitments with state.nonce, as any private block. A reader verifies it once it holds it; a node waits on a block whose author's genesis it lacks, as for any need. A genesis has no public header: a reader outside its audience is sent nothing of it.
genesis.recovery_about: recovery_key_hash and recovery_reach come together or not at all, and only in a genesis: no key grant names them (identity.md, The recovery key)
genesis.recognised: An actor is judged as a genesis when it has state.public_key_sign or has no refs.author; it is then held to this list alone (bad_genesis), and its signature must open with its own public_key_sign (bad_genesis, never bad_signature).
genesis.optional_about: Besides `required`, a genesis may carry suite, public_key_encrypt and custodian (key_fields, all but roles), the recovery fields (recovery) and, when its audience is a list, its nonce (private); never roles, name or marks (bad_genesis).

required.about: What a block needs beyond the common five (core.md, section 7), by its role: a block that starts something needs the fields of its type; a block that replies to another needs refs.answers (or, for the author's own stop, refs.updates) and state.status.

transfer: one of refs.to_owner, refs.to_holder, refs.to_place, state.count

replies.unless: the reply is a counter-offer: a promise with refs.answers whose state carries new terms and no status (promises.md, Answers)

fields.about: The base fields of the closed types. Every closed type may also carry `every`. A closed block says more only through a schema it names (core.md, section 7). The open types (thing, observe, transform and any new word) list nothing here: their fields are described by the base schemas (spec/schemas), and nothing is refused for them.

key_fields.about: Defined once. A genesis (actor) carries them, a key grant carries them, and a member grant and a circle's actor carry roles. A genesis may carry all but roles, and the recovery pair (genesis.recovery); a field that is not a key field is the type's own (fields).

shapes.price_figure_about: A price fixed later (promises.md, Terms): `figure` the kind of `observe` whose `state.money` is the figure, `by` the readers (ids or circle#role), `signers` how many different ones must have signed the same figure, `deadline` and `keepers` the window on a named clock, and optionally `fraction` (a decimal from 0 to 1: the share of the figure the price is), `min` and `max` (money: a figure outside them does not count). It is a bare price's shape, never a line's.

where.values: decimal strings; radius is an amount in m

shapes.money_about: currency is an ISO 4217 code (grammar.currency) or a currency_unit: issuer an id (grammar.id) whose published schema defines the unit, unit its name, decimals an integer 0 to limits.decimals_max. Money in different currencies is never added or compared by the protocol.
shapes.when_window_about: Any of these, at least one, alone or beside the keys of a range or a relative form; not_before and not_after are times, takes a duration (blocks.md, profiles/tasks.md).
shapes.when_event_about: A `when` that follows an event is { after, wait } with `after` an observe kind (any text that is not an id): due `wait` after the receiving side's observe of that kind `for` the promise, dated by the named clock (promises.md, Relative time). `after` an id is the relative form of a block.
shapes.keepers_about: A named clock (blocks.md): `names` a non-empty list of ids or circle#role, `needed` by Counts (folds.md): a set of one needs none, a larger set states it. It sits in a condition `without` and in a promise's terms.

places.about: A shape is read only at a place the protocol gives it, never by a field name deeper in. The places are the fields of a block's state, of its terms and scope, and of each item of its lines and split. A value at a place is read by its own keys, and the fields that `field_shape` gives the shape `shape` hold an object, never a bare value. A map nested under a field is data: nothing in it is read as a shape. The fields named in data are not places: what they hold is data (a schema's fields, grounds and roles name things, and the items of shares are data no fold reads), so nothing in them is read as a shape.

field_shape_about: Which shape a field name holds, where the protocol gives it a place (shapes.places): time (grammar.time; `when` also takes the forms of shapes.when), date (grammar.date), duration (grammar.duration), shape (exactly one of the keyed shapes in `shapes`, never a bare value). The lists a check asks for (every time field, every duration field) are read from this table.

grammar.id_about: A bare id is SHA-256. Any other hash carries its name and a colon (suites, hashes).

grammar_notes.about: Every pattern is an ECMAScript regular expression, anchored at both ends: `$` means the end of the text, never before a final newline. A reader in another engine anchors the end exactly (Python: re.fullmatch, or \Z), or a value with a trailing newline would pass.
grammar_notes.duration: Written without lookahead so every regex engine runs it.
grammar_notes.time: The pattern is the shape; the value must also be a real calendar instant (no 30 February).
grammar_notes.zone: Shaped like an IANA time zone name: a name with no slash (UTC, and the legacy names GMT, CET, EST5EDT, Zulu), or Area/Location with one or two slashes (Europe/London, America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires). The protocol checks the shape, never a list of zones.
grammar_notes.rrule_part: One part of an RRULE value (RFC 5545), KEY=VALUE; the parts are joined by ; and exactly one is FREQ, from repeat.freq.
grammar_notes.date: The pattern is the shape; the value must also be a real calendar date.

hashes_about: A hash name a reader knows is the bare SHA-256 and every `prefix` of a hash that a suite in `suites` (not `future`) uses: sm3. sha3-256 is listed for the future suite and is unknown until that suite is fixed in vectors.

suites.about: A suite names a hash, a signature algorithm and an envelope together. A key names its suite in state.suite; left out, std. A block is hashed with the hash of the suite of the key that signed it. A reader refuses an unknown suite (refusals.codes.block.unknown_suite).

passkey.form: r then s (64 bytes), the length of authenticatorData (2 bytes, big-endian), authenticatorData, clientDataJSON
passkey.challenge: base64url, no padding, of SHA-256 of the signed bytes (for a block, its id)

sm.key_about: SM4 takes 16 bytes: the content key is the first 16 of its 32 random bytes and HKDF derives 16 bytes (privacy.md, Envelope).

pq.status: noted, not usable until sizes are fixed in vectors; a signature must still fit limits.block_bytes

messages.public_block_about: No suite: a block is hashed in the suite of the key that signed it (core.md, sections 2 and 6), so a message that names one is refused (bad_hash), and so is a CBOR message with anything after the signature. A message carries no version: one that does is refused (shape).
messages.proof_about: A signed request carries exactly one of counter (an integer above the highest the node has seen from the signer) or challenge (issued by the node, used once). It carries no time.
messages.push_answer_order: taken: round order, ascending by hash inside a round (blocks arriving as the other half of a sealed block held count as the first round). refused: the same, a block's codes in the order of refusals.codes.block. waiting: ascending by hash, each needs ascending. equivocations: each pair sorted, the list sorted. held, when given: ascending by hash.
messages.signature_about: A node signs an answer, and a signer a request, over the UTF-8 canonical JSON of the object without its `signature` key. A pull answer's `request` is the bare SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON of the whole signed request, `signature` included. header_signature signs the canonical JSON of `header`. An envelope plaintext is the canonical JSON of the plaintext object.

peers.about: Three peers: micro, edge, node. A micro that acts and an index are variants.
peers.micro_clockless: a micro may leave out at and when on observe, transform and transfer; its edge writes an observe of kind receipt

optional_profiles.about: Optional. A node that has never heard of a profile still accepts every block in it.

successor_view.input: a successor grant, arrivals on this node, the reader's clock

output.events: the standing event observes, one per witness, sorted
output.cancelled: the event observes the person defeated in time, sorted
output.since: the arrival of the needed-th event, or null
output.fired: true once the reader's clock reaches fires

successor.close_rule: A close counts when its author is not the person and signs it under a successor grant the person gave in their own name to them, that no stop or decline in the close's causal past has ended, with the triggers of needed listed witnesses under it in the close's causal past and none defeated by the person, and no counted close of its author in its causal past (a dead successor closes no one). A counted close ends authority, never a promise: from that block on, every grant the person gave in their own name, not as a circle and not their successor grant (for blocks that have the close in their causal past), and the person's membership of every circle, except what state.continues names (grants, a circle or a member grant the successor carries on). An observe is an open type: continues needs no declaring.

counted_in.input: a ballot result, a commitment, the named counter
counted_in.output: true when the result is signed by that counter and lists the commitment in counted

output.epoch: the current epoch; 0 is the circle actor's key
output.keys: the encryption keys of the epoch's counted rekeys, sorted

residency.regions: plain labels the node's promise and the author's request name, compared by exact equality; the protocol gives none a meaning

legacy.about: Not part of the protocol. No node reads an older shape.

refusals.about: Every refusal is { hash, code, detail }: code from these lists, detail free text for people. block: why a node refuses a block's bytes (final for those bytes), or, for unmet, why it waits. fold: why a fold counts a block for nothing. message: why a node refuses a pull or push. valid runs the checks in `checks` in order and stops at the first check that finds anything; its refusal is every code that check found, one per code, in the order of the block codes below.

block.not_canonical: not in canonical form: key or set order, NFC, null, duplicate keys, a repeat in a set, or not exactly type, state and refs
block.float: a number with a fraction or exponent in signed content
block.integer_range: a whole number outside integers.min..integers.max, or -0
block.decimal: a decimal string outside grammar.decimal, or with more digits than limits.decimal_digits
block.grammar: an id, salt, nonce, role ref, language tag, type name, RRULE or time zone outside its grammar
block.time: a time, date or duration outside its grammar
block.calendar: a time or date in the right shape that is not a real calendar instant
block.shape: an amount, money, price, range, mark, share, split, when, where or reveal without its keys; a refrain flag, a needed or removal rule, a role list item or an event repeat not in its shape
block.type_name: a type that does not match grammar.type_name
block.size_limit: its canonical body is over limits.block_bytes (a sealed copy's block, once opened), or it nests deeper than limits.depth
block.after_limit: refs.after names more than limits.after_heads heads
block.audience: an audience that is neither public nor a sorted list of commitments
block.bad_genesis: a genesis with author, prev, after or seq, missing a genesis field, with only one of the recovery fields, or not signed by its own key
block.chain: a seq or prev that does not fit its key's chain, or a skip that goes backwards
block.at_missing: no at on a block that is not an observe, transform or transfer
block.unmet: the block rests on blocks the checker does not hold (its author's genesis, its prev, the grant it acts under, a grant's parent, counted_to, or the block it answers or updates, a promise's answered or updated promise, the schema it names: needs): not a refusal but a wait; judged once, when they arrive
block.bad_hash: an id sent with it is not the hash of its canonical bytes in the suite of the key that signed it (no label names the suite)
block.bad_signature: its signature opens with no key of its author
block.unknown_suite: a key that names a suite the reader does not know, or a key, signature or id outside its suite's grammar
block.not_own_rotation: a rotation signed by none of the key it replaces, the recovery key, or the operator of an agent or machine
block.recovery_scope: the recovery key signed something other than a key grant or a defeats a profile gives it
block.required: a closed block missing a required field (core.md, section 7): a refrain without until, a to_role without refs.to, a rekey without refs.as
block.undeclared_ref: on a closed type, a ref key neither shared nor declared by its schema
block.undeclared_field: on a closed type, a state field neither its type's base field nor declared by its schema
block.status_not_answer: a status on a block that neither answers nor updates its author's own
block.bad_status: a status not in statuses, stopped without a valid stop, or a stop beside any other status or none
block.deal_not_named: an answer or counter in a deal that does not name the deal's first promise, exactly, in refs.for
block.lines: a line without an id unique in the promise, a top-level price or quantity beside lines, or refs.what not the lines' what
block.wider_than_parent: a child grant's scope or depth wider than its parent's on any field
block.not_receiver: a grant passed on by someone other than its parent's receiver, or, for a parent made to a circle, by a block not signed as that circle
block.bad_roles: a circle roles list whose powers are not in powers (or a profile's powers) or repeat one, a role name that is empty, repeated or holds #, or a founder with no first role

fold.not_a_side: signed by neither side nor an agent under a side's live grant
fold.open_offer_counter: a counter to an open offer, by the taker or the offerer in a chain of counters: it ends nothing (only the author ends an open offer) and binds nothing until the side that did not sign it answers it accepted; that accept of a counter of the chain is an allocation, a one-to-one deal on the counter's own terms whose quantity counts against the open offer's
fold.not_live: acts under a grant that is not live, or outside its scope (its acts by exact name, its parties), or is an act that moves things or binds someone with no trusted schema saying undo ok and neither a specific accepted ask nor a grant naming it with a limit (a commitment to one, or a visible one)
fold.no_role: signs as a circle without a role with the sign power, in the circle's fold of its causal past
fold.not_counted: a settling block the receiver has not accepted and no confirmer the grounds name has confirmed
fold.equivocation: one of a pair that name one prev, or a later block of that key: proof, counted for nothing of what is owed to its signer
fold.quote_only: an accept of a quote request: an agent's ask whose grant does not name the act binds no one

message.bad_signature: the message is not signed by the signer it names
message.replay: its counter is not above the highest seen, or its challenge was not issued or was used
message.not_admitted: the node's admission rule does not admit it
message.not_human: a first block to a stranger signed by an agent, outside the order channel the receiver's rule states

identity.input: an id and the blocks held

output.signed_by_author: { hash: true when the block is the id's }
output.frozen: the frozen keys among them, sorted
output.operators: authors of live operator grants naming it, sorted

promise_stage.input: a first promise, or an allocation (promises.md), and the blocks held; no clock. A promise that rests on blocks not held, one that speaks for neither side, or an allocation the open offer does not bind has no stage (null)

output.stage: offered, asked, declined, stopped, accepted, underway, done, reversed or breached (the view adds expired, and elapsed for a refrain whose until has passed)
output.from: the onward stop's hash, or the counted defeats by the deal's referee that breached a refrain (null when its signal condition breached it)
output.by: on a stage stopped onward, the side that ended it: from, to, or both (the other side confirms the stop, or the first stops, which do not see each other, are one by each side); else null
output.offer: the offer the binding accept answers; with none, the live offer when there is only one, else null
output.live: every live offer, sorted (two counters to one offer both stand)
output.accept: the binding accept's hash, or null
output.quantity: the quantity chosen, an amount (the accept's, else the allocation's, else the terms'; a range is what may be chosen, never a choice), or null; on an open offer, the sum its allocations bind
output.takers: [{ who, request, allocation, quantity, over_allocated }] on an open offer, in causal order; in an allocation's own deal, that one taker
output.forks: allocations that do not see one before them, or accepts of live offers that do not see each other: proof of a lie, sorted. A lie never frees the liar: each allocation still binds its taker, and of crossing accepts the same terms bind, else the one the other side's act names
output.lines: [{ id, needed, moved }], id null without lines
output.total: money the price comes to, or null (minor past 2^53 - 1 is exact decimal text)
output.paid: money counted to the from side, by what the from side's own accepted answers say each payment covers (state.covers), else its own money; in the price's currency, else the one currency the payments cover; or null (minor past 2^53 - 1 is exact decimal text)
output.stopped: occurrence start times or hashes stopped, sorted
output.disputed: [{ hash, of, by, at }]: each counted defeats by a side of a block in the deal that is not its own (by: from or to; at: the date it gives, or null), sorted by hash then of. It changes nothing: only the deal's referee changes the stage
output.due: the deal's terms.pay_by, or null (always null on a standing promise: it is due occurrence by occurrence, in occurrences)
output.paid_at: once the price is paid in full, the latest date among the payments, each dated by the first counting answer of the side it is paid to (or a named confirmer's confirms); else null (always null on a standing promise)
output.uncovered: money { minor, currency } or null: on a deal stopped onward, breached or over-allocated and not done, what was paid and sent for it, less what was paid back, less the price of what moved to the payer, less terms.forfeit; never below zero; null when nothing was paid. The payer's claim shown as a fact: it changes no stage
output.over_allocated: true when the offerer's allocations, in causal order with the stopped ones left out, pass what the open offer offered (an allocation's deal: this one does); on the open offer, when any does. A fact: it changes no stage
output.owed: null until a hand-over of what is owed counts (promises.md, Owed); then { to, from: [{ owner, money }], forked }: to the owner of what moves, from the owners of the price and their parts sorted by owner, forked the hand-overs a fork of one key voids
output.received_at: [{ message, side, at }]: each counted observe of kind message a side wrote for the deal, with the time the named clock received it (the promise's keepers, and no one else's receipt); at null while there is no clock or no receipt. A fact: money paid for a deal that failed is owed back from the failure, no intent needed; "knowing" starts only when a notice reached the keeper
output.moved: [{ pay_by, proposal, answer }]: each new date both sides signed (a side's observe of kind message for the deal with a pay_by, answered accepted by an observe of the other side), in the order the answers stand in causal order. The first promise's own pay_by stays in due; a date only one side signed is not listed
output.owed_on: [{ from, to, money, payment }]: a counted payment made, unseen by its payer, to an owner who had handed that part on: the old owner holds that amount for the new one; sorted by payment, then to
output.referee_ties: [{ referee, side, how }]: each name on the deal's bench tied to a side (decision H9), read from the blocks held: side from or to; how role (a role inside the side's circle), member (a member of the side's circle) or operator (an autonomous system the side runs); sorted by referee, side, how; empty until a binding accept exists. A fact: it changes no stage
output.occurrences: on a standing promise, [{ occurrence, due, paid, paid_at }] for each occurrence a counted payment names (state.occurrence) or an event started, sorted: due is its start time, or an event's at plus the repeat's wait; paid what its payments put toward the price; paid_at, once that covers one occurrence's price, the latest date among them. Empty on any other promise
output.price_fixed: null when the price is a plain number; for a price fixed later (promises.md, Terms), false until it is fixed (total is then null and the price is never paid), true once `signers` readers have each signed the same figure in time. A fact: it changes no stage

circle_state.input: a circle and the blocks held

output.removed: { id: null }: every id that is out (a circle reads no counted_to)

may_act_as.input: a block, a circle, a role or none
may_act_as.output: with no role, true when the block is signed as the circle and its author holds the sign power through a role in the circle's fold of the block's causal past; with a role, true when its author holds that role there (a grant to a role, authority.md), signed as the circle or not; false for a block outside a cut of its author's ended grant

members_then.input: a block and a circle or circle#role
members_then.output: the member or holder ids, sorted

where_now.output: the places (hashes), sorted; empty when none is known

output.owner: an id, or null after a transfer to an open receiver
output.transfers: the counted ownership transfers, in order
output.conflict: the crossing pair, sorted, or null

output.standing: [{ share, owner }] the shares that stand on it: things of kind share that name it in refs.subject, made by whoever owned it where the share stands
output.nothing: [{ share, reason }] shares that count for nothing: not_a_thing (the subject is no thing), kind (some thing names it in refs.of), not_owner (the maker did not own it there)

use_shown.input: a place, the blocks held, and optionally a named clock (keepers)

output.clock: keepers when a clock was named, else author (each use is dated by its author's own at)
output.users: [{ user, acts, count, unreceived, first, last, seasons, bounds, resting, overlaps, leave }] sorted by user; none means no use in what the reader holds. `leave` is null, or { of, since, until }: the owner's live grant of kind leave to this user for the place, shown as by leave of `of` since `since`, never as a use that stands against the owner

not_free_shown.input: a block and the blocks held

output.shown: [{ block, by, reason, threat, at }] the signer's own words (observe of kind not_free) naming the block in refs.subject, written by the block's author; a claim shown beside the block, never a verdict
output.nothing: [{ block, why }] words by anyone else (why: not_signer): their own observes

invasion_shown.input: a claim of invasion (an observe of kind invasion) and the blocks held

output.holder: who holds the claim now: the claimant, then each accepted hand-over
output.standing: harmed (the holder owns, or holds a share of, the thing crossed, or is the person crossed), holds (the harmed party handed the claim over), or none
output.evidence: the claim's derives_from, sorted; empty means evidence: none
output.accused: [{ who, named, accepted }] each accused with the judges he named and the claimant's judges he answered accepted (silence is never an accept)
output.judges: [{ judge, named_by }] judges named by a grant of kind referee for the claim, by the holder side or an accused
output.rulings: [{ block, judge, named_by, word, up_to, evidence }] a named judge's confirms or defeats of the claim; up_to only on a confirms
output.nothing: [{ block, reason }] a ruling or naming that counts for nothing: side (a claimant, an accused or one who speaks for either), not_named

chain.input: the blocks of one signing key, and the id of the block that brought that key in
chain.head: hash of the block with the highest seq, or null when two share it
chain.length: the key's blocks, leaving out the members of every equivocation pair; later blocks of the key count (they bind their signer)
chain.gaps: seq numbers missing that no skip block explains: the lowest first, at most limits.gaps_max
chain.equivocations: pairs of hashes naming one prev, each pair sorted
chain.broken: hashes whose prev does not name the block before
chain.ok: true when there are no unexplained gaps, equivocations or broken links

next_link.seq: the next seq for the key
next_link.prev: the hash of the key's previous block, or of the block that brought the key in

consent.input: a person, a sender (or none), optionally the hash of the grant the sender's block acts under (refs.under), and the blocks held

output.word: yes, stop, keep or move, or null
output.block: the consent block that decides (the lowest hash of tied blocks that agree), or null

consent.about: The person's own blocks count for every word; anyone else's counts only as a stop that binds the recorder's own side, or as a yes that lifts a stop that same recorder recorded and has it in its causal past (consent.md). A stop wins any tie; a tie of other words gives null. There is no public list.

release_shown.input: a deal's first promise or a thing, and the blocks held

output.subject: the block asked about
output.released: [{ block, by, side, to }] counted releases (an observe of kind release) that let go of the signer's own claims on it: one naming it in refs.subject, or, for a deal, a general release by a side to the other side that has it in its causal past and does not list it in state.except; side is from (owed the price) or to (owed what moves), null for a thing; sorted by block
output.kept_open: [{ block, by, side }] general releases that list the deal in state.except: the debt stays open; sorted by block

bids_shown.input: a deal's first promise (the quarrel) and the blocks held; null for any other block

output.currency: the currency both bids state, or null
output.in: the sides (from, to) whose sealed bid counts: one bid each, the same deadline, clock and currency, received by the deadline on the named clock; sorted
output.opened: the sides whose opening counts (it opens the commitment, signed by the same side, received by the deadline); sorted. The numbers themselves are never shown
output.overlap: null until both sides have opened; then true when the to side's number (the most it would pay) is at least the from side's (the least it would take), else false
output.middle: money { minor, currency }, the mean of the two numbers rounded half up, only on an overlap; else null

folds_about: Every fold has: ops (the door ops that answer it), over (what it is asked of: a promise, a thing, a key, a circle, a circle_role, an `as` block, a person), and words (the outputs that are words, core.md section 11, or "all"; every other output is a reading). The audit, the fuzzer and the simulation check every fold listed here (and the views that name an over), and fail on one they cannot ask.

views.about: A view reads a fold and the reader's clock or arrivals, and says whose.

promise_view.input: a first promise, the blocks held, the reader's clock, and optionally the reader's arrivals with `unknown_arrival` (then every block is read with signed_by_author as the recovery_reach view reads it)
promise_view.output: the promise_stage answer, with stage expired once the clock passes expires and nothing binds, and a refrain that is accepted or underway elapsed once the clock passes its until (decision H15: a fact of its term, never done; what was paid is in paid); beside the stage, `condition`: holds, not or unread for the offer's terms.condition, null with none; `condition_failed`: when the condition does not hold, the first promise of the deal it names that ended without it (stopped, declined, expired or breached) or that itself rests on one, else null (failure spreads visibly, never just open); `missed`: the dates in force in the order agreed (the first promise's pay_by, then each date both sides signed, in `moved`) that passed before the price was paid in full, or before the reader's clock while it is unpaid; null with no pay_by or on a standing promise

ownership_view.input: an instance, the blocks held, the reader's arrivals and unknown_arrival, and the reader's clock
ownership_view.output: the ownership fold's answer, read with signed_by_author as the recovery_reach view reads it: a sale the reach protects stands for this reader (the fold stays the word); a transfer that carries a condition (state.condition) counts once the condition holds at the clock given (none given: only a condition that needs no clock)

live_grant.clock: the node that relies on the act, when it takes the block in
live_grant.input: an act block, its grants, that clock
live_grant.output: true when every grant's scope.until is later than the clock

recovery_reach.input: a recovery rotation, the identity fold, the reader's arrivals and unknown_arrival
recovery_reach.output: the blocks of a recovery rotation's identity that the fold voids and the reader's arrivals restore (a block the reach protects, and what a protected key grant brought in), sorted; asked about any other block, none

withdrawal_seen.input: a withdrawal, a counterparty block, its node's arrivals
withdrawal_seen.output: true when the withdrawal is in the block's causal past, or the node records any arrival of it (no times are compared)

due.clock: the performer's own, from the anchor's arrival on its node
due.input: a promise with a relative when, the performer's arrivals and clock
due.output: the instant it falls due, or null while the anchor has not arrived

pot.clock: the reader's own, when a payout's condition reads it (none given: only a condition that needs none)
pot.input: a first promise (the head), the blocks held, and the reader's clock (a payout's condition may read it)

output.currency: the pot's currency: the backing's, else the lowest pay-in's; null for a count pot or when neither exists
output.unit: the pot's unit when it counts a named kind (an amount): the backing's, else the lowest pay-in's; null for a money pot
output.backing: terms.backing, the holder's own word, in minor units (money) or a decimal text (a count); null when the head's terms.cap is all (no limit)
output.cap: all when the head's terms.cap is the word all (written out, never a default: all the holder owns on the day a claim is read, the referee fixing the sum; backing and left are then null and a payout is never past the pot), else null
output.paid_in: the pay-ins: money transfers for the head to the holder, accepted by the holder
output.left: backing plus paid_in (only while the head's terms say pay_in kept) less paid_out, never below zero; null when cap is all
output.pay_in: the head's terms.pay_in: kept (a premium: leaving takes nothing back), held (it comes back in full and is never paid out while held), or null when the terms say neither (the card shows 'pay-in: not said'; nothing is filled in)
output.held_back: the pay-ins held back from payouts: paid_in when pay_in is held, else zero
output.payouts: [{ block, to, money | amount, counts, why }] the holder's money (or amount) transfers for the head to a named receiver who accepted; why is null, past_the_pot, unseen_together, not_confirmed or not_holder

condition_holds.input: a condition, the blocks held, the reader's clock
condition_holds.output: true or false for the shapes the protocol reads (condition_shapes; promises.md, Conditions); null for any other shape (not read)

reading_condition_holds.input: a reading_condition, the blocks held, the reader's clock
reading_condition_holds.output: whether the readings the condition names hold by the reader's clock (profiles/tasks.md)

door.about: The door is the one call every implementation answers: an op name and positional arguments (JSON), and a result (JSON). spec/vectors.json `door` holds one or more cases per op below: `args`, then `expect` (a subset match: every key given must match, extra keys in a result do not matter; a list or text must match exactly when the case says `exact`, and lists are compared in order), or `codes` (the refusal codes, in order), or `error`. An implementation conforms when it answers every case. An op outside this table is outside the protocol.

conventions.block: { type, state, refs }: a block as written (core.md, section 1).
conventions.full_block: a block with its `hash` (its id), its `signature` (hex) and, when its key's suite is not std, `suite`: { hash, type, state, refs, signature, suite? }. This is what an op that takes blocks held, a story or a store reads. Order in a list of held blocks never matters.
conventions.id: a hash: 64 lowercase hex (or a hash name and colon first). `time`: the text of core.md, section 3. `arrivals`: an object { hash: time } of when this reader's node took each block in; null or a missing hash means unknown. A reader of the recovery reach (`unknown_arrival`) says whether it reads an unknown arrival `inside` the reach (the rotation voids the block) or `outside` it (the block arrived before the reach began); the protocol picks neither, and arrivals without it are an argument error. `clock` or `now`: a time; anything else (other than null where the clock may be left out) is an argument error, never read as a time. A list argument (written `[...]` in an op's args) given as anything but a list, or null, is an argument error, never read as the empty list.
conventions.refusals: a list of { code, detail }. A case with `codes` compares the codes only, in the order of protocol.json refusals.codes. Details are free text.
conventions.keys: public keys and signatures are hex as in core.md, section 2; a private key is the seed hex for p256 and sm, and for std the seed, which `keypair` also writes as PKCS#8 DER hex (`302e020100300506032b657004220420` then the 32 seed bytes).
conventions.suite_arg: an optional suite name, default std

args: seed: 64 hex (the 32-byte seed of core.md, section 2)

suite_of_key.result: the suite whose SPKI prefix the key starts with, else null

sign.result: signature hex over the canonical bytes of the block (core.md, section 2: deterministic)

verify.result: true when the signature opens (a passkey signature included); the suite is the key's

hash.result: the id of that block in that suite

id_of.result: the block's id: the hash of its canonical bytes in the suite of the key that signed it (core.md, section 2), that key found among `held`; without `held`, the suite the block shows (a genesis's own, else its prev's hash)

valid.result: refusals (core.md, section 8); empty when valid. `held` is the context: valid reads only what the block rests on in it, and no arrival or clock

args: text: the block as JSON text
strict_text.result: what the bytes alone say, with no context: `not_canonical` for text that breaks canonical.md (a repeated key, a lone surrogate) or is not exactly { type, state, refs }, else the refusal of the first of checks 2, 3 and 4, else of check 8 (core.md, section 8)

args: text: a push { messages, for } as JSON text, as it arrived
strict_push.result: for each message in order, what its block's bytes alone say (as `strict_text`; a sealed message has none): a node reads a push from its text, so a repeated key or a number written as a float is never normalised away. Text with a repeated key anywhere, or that is not a push, is an argument error (transport.md)

refusals.result: refusals of `check` (core.md, section 8): checks 1 to 4 and 8, all codes found

needs.result: the ids the block rests on (protocol.json needs), sorted ascending; with `held`, only those not held

recovery_key_hash.result: identity.md: the suite's hash of the key's SPKI hex as UTF-8 text

wrap.result: the message { block, signature } (core.md, section 6): never a suite, never a version

unwrap.result: the full block { hash, type, state, refs, signature }; the id is recomputed, in the suite of the key that signed it (core.md, section 2): with `held`, the author's key that opens it; without, the suite the block shows (a genesis's own, else its prev's hash). A message that names a suite is an error (bad_hash); one that carries a version is an error (shape)

header.result: the public header { author, seq, prev, hash } with `withheld` or `skip` when the block says so (privacy.md)

args: fixed?: { vectorsOnly: true, ephemeral, contentKey, nonce, keyNonces } (fixed randomness only reproduces a vector; without vectorsOnly: true it is an argument error)
seal.result: the envelope (privacy.md); `fixed` gives the random values (hex, the ephemeral private key, content key, content nonce, one key nonce per recipient) so a case is exact; with none the values are random

open.result: the plaintext JSON; a recipient it is not for is an error

cbor_encode.result: lowercase hex of the CBOR message [t, block, signature] (encoding.md); `short` uses key table 1 and t = 1

cbor_decode.result: the full block; the id is recomputed from the canonical JSON, in the suite of the key that signed it (as unwrap). Anything after the signature is an error

passkey_challenge.result: the WebAuthn challenge for the block: base64url, no padding, of the 32 bytes of SHA-256 of its canonical bytes, which is its id for a std or p256 key (encoding.md, Passkeys)

verify_message.result: true when `signature` opens over the canonical JSON of the object without `signature` (nodes.md)

args: unknown_arrival: `inside` or `outside` the reach, required with arrivals (what the reader reads a block whose arrival it does not know as)
key_timeline.result: [{ key, by, signer, frozen, suite }]: every key the identity fold knows but a void one (identity.md), in the order of the blocks that brought them in (by the size of each one's causal past, then `seq`, then hash), `by` the block that brought it in (the genesis for the genesis key), `signer` the key that signed that block (null for the genesis key, `recovery` for the recovery key, `operator` for an operator's key grant)

args: unknown_arrival: `inside` or `outside` the reach, required with arrivals (what the reader reads a block whose arrival it does not know as)
recovery_reach.result: the voided blocks the reach protects (identity.md), sorted

args: last: full_block of the key's chain, or null
next_link.result: { seq, prev }: the next place in the key's chain (core.md, section 5)

args: brought_in: id of the block that brought the key in
check_chain.result: { head, length, gaps, skips, equivocations, broken, ok } (folds.md, chain)

fork_pairs.result: the equivocating pairs, each sorted, the list sorted (nodes.md)

past_of.result: the ids in its causal past (blocks.md), sorted

sees.result: true when `earlier` is in the causal past of `later`

matches.result: true when the block matches the pull filter (nodes.md, Pull)

due.result: the instant it falls due (the anchor's arrival plus `wait`), or null while the anchor has not arrived

args: { } (no options: a stage is a function of the blocks alone)
promise_stage.result: the promise_stage answer of protocol.json folds (folds.md)

promise_views.result: { id: the promise_view answer }: many deals of one store, read against one reading of it

promise_view.result: the same answer, with stage `expired` as folds.md says; with arrivals, every block read as the recovery reach view reads it (decision c9)

args: unknown_arrival: `inside` or `outside` the reach, required with arrivals (what the reader reads a block whose arrival it does not know as)
ownership_view.result: { owner, transfers, conflict } as the view `ownership_view` (folds.md, Views)

live_grant.result: true when every grant's scope.until is later than the clock

may_act_as.result: true or false (folds.md); no code is returned

under_ok.result: true when the block speaks for its grantor under the grant it names (refs.under): the grant is held, is for its signer, is live, covers the act, and an act that moves things or binds is not irreversible, or has what that needs (authority.md); no clock is read

args: now?: the reader's clock for a conditioned transfer (null reads none that needs a clock)
ownership.result: { owner, transfers, conflict } as the fold `ownership` (folds.md); a transfer with state.condition counts only when its condition holds (things.md, Transfers)

where_now.result: the places (hashes), sorted; empty when none is known (folds.md)

shares_on.result: { standing, nothing } as the fold `shares_on` (folds.md, Shares standing on a thing)

args: keepers?: a named clock, { names, needed } (null dates each use by its author's own at)
use_shown.result: { clock, users } as the fold `use_shown` (folds.md, Uses shown)

not_free_shown.result: { shown, nothing } as the fold `not_free_shown` (folds.md, Words beside a block)

invasion_shown.result: null, or the fold `invasion_shown` (folds.md, A claim of invasion shown)

args: now?: the reader's clock (null reads no condition that needs one)
pot.result: null, or the fold `pot` (folds.md, A pot)

args: within?: a block, to read the circle as of its causal past
circle_state.result: { founder, members, removed } or null when the circle is not held, or within a block whose causal past does not hold it (folds.md)

args: under?: grant id the sender's block acts under
admission: { parties?, per_stranger?, order_channel? } as the node's rule states it, or null for no rule; stated, never defaulted
strangers_today: integer (stated, never defaulted), blocks this node took today from this block's sender, when it is not in parties (each sender is counted alone: decision D17)
long?: true for the ten-character form
receipt_code.result: the code of profiles/short-form.md: XXXX-XXXX, or XXXXX-XXXXX when long

args: text: a code as a person types it
code_matches.result: true when the text names the block: case, spaces and hyphens ignored, O read as 0, I and L as 1; eight characters match the short code, ten the long one

earnest_shape_ok.result: true when it has exactly those keys, money a money shape and holder an id

args: choices: { takes_pairs: boolean }, the node's own stated choice (nodes.md, A node's promise): with true the blocks of a forked pair arriving together, or forking one held, are taken as well as listed in equivocations, with false neither is taken; no default
accept.result: { taken: [id], waiting: [{ hash, needs: [id] }], refused: [{ hash, code, detail }], equivocations: [[id, id]] } in the order nodes.md, Push, fixes

args: choices: { takes_pairs: boolean }, the node's own stated choice: with true the blocks of a forked pair arriving together are taken as well as listed in equivocations, with false neither is taken; no default
accept_sealed.result: the same shape as `accept`, judged from the public headers (privacy.md)

args: log: [{ n, block, header?, header_signature?, copies? }]

choices: { cap: integer of at least 1, serves_pairs: boolean }, the node's own stated choices (nodes.md, A node's promise): the most blocks one answer carries (a pull's limit is cut to it), and whether the other half of a forked pair is sent with an answer that includes one; no default
through?: the last arrival number the node read to answer, or null
answer_pull.result: { node, request, blocks: [{ n, message }], next, signature } (nodes.md, Pull); `signature` only when a private key is given; an answer that is not full has `next` at least `through`

convert.result: outside the protocol (legacy/converter.md); a case carries `oracle: false`

merkle_root.result: encoding.md, Large content: the Merkle root (64 hex) over the chunks; an error (argument) for no chunks

merkle_proof.result: the proof of that chunk: the sibling hashes (hex) from the leaf up; an error (argument) for an index that is no chunk

merkle_verify.result: true when the block's `state.marks` holds exactly one `{ scheme: "merkle", value }` mark, `state.chunks` (its signed count) is an integer of at least 1, and the proof shows the chunk is chunk `index` of that many under that root; the count is never an argument

args: each: money or amount or null
limit_commitment.result: authority.md, The limit is the principal's fence: the commitment (privacy.md) to the canonical JSON of { limit, every, each } (every and each left out when null), the value of a grant's `scope.limit_commitment`

limit_opens.result: true when the observe is of kind `limit`, `refs.for` the grant, carries a salt and a `limit` or an `each`, and its `limit`, `every`, `each` and `salt` commit to the grant's `scope.limit_commitment`; false when the grant has none

args: quantity: the quantity chosen, or null for the terms' own
terms_total.result: folds.md, stage 2: what the terms come to, { minor, currency } (lines in the first line's currency added up; minor past 2^53 - 1 is exact decimal text), or null when a price has no total or nothing is priced

args: fence: the limit observe, its state, or a limit
spent: minor units or the amount's value, a whole number or a decimal string (default 0)
within_limit.result: authority.md, The limit is the principal's fence: true when spent plus value is within the limit and value within each, compared exactly, in the same currency or unit; false otherwise, and for a spent that is not a number

args: child: the child grant's limit observe, its state, or { limit, every, each }
parent: the parent grant's, the same way
at: a time, the parent grant's at
limit_within_parent.result: authority.md, What a reader can check about a child's sealed limit: true when each of the parent's limit and each the child has too, in the same currency or unit and no larger (compared exactly), and, where the parent has an every, the child's is no shorter, both added to at; false otherwise

args: limit: money or amount or null
each: money or amount or null
limit_fence.result: the observe of kind limit for the grant, as { type, state, refs, audience } to hand to write, its audience the agent alone

base_fields.result: the base fields of that type, beside `every`: the list in `fields`, or none for an open type

condition_holds.result: promises.md, Conditions: whether a condition holds on the blocks held at the reader's clock (condition_shapes: settled, accepted, deed, a reading, a signal, paid, opened or without)

cbor.about: Compact form of a public block (encoding.md). The id is always the hash of the canonical JSON; CBOR is transport only. At year zero the key table is reset: this is table 1.

bytes.about: A value at one of these paths that matches its grammar is a byte string; otherwise text (an id with a hash prefix stays text). `[]` is each element, `*` any key. hash: 32 bytes. sign_key: std 32 raw bytes (suites.std.sign_key.spki_prefix put back), other suites the whole SPKI. encrypt_key: the suite's raw bytes. nonce: 16 bytes.

cbor.time: A value at a time field (time_fields, in time_fields_checked_in) matching grammar.time is an integer of milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z; when.from and when.to likewise.

message.header_about: A chain header has exactly the four keys. seq is an integer; the three ids are 32-byte byte strings when bare, text when they carry a hash prefix.

condition_shapes_about: The condition shapes the protocol reads (promises.md, Conditions), each named by its key: settled (that promise is done, or a refrain elapsed with nothing owed), accepted (that deal binds: its stage is accepted or further along, read from the promise fold; decision H17), deed (that block is held and counts), reading (a sensor's readings, profiles/tasks.md), signal (named signers' observes), paid (that deal's price is paid in full: the price side of the deal, so a transfer of title may wait for the price without waiting for the goods), opened (a counted block carries the opening of a commitment, privacy.md: someone shows the code) and, wrapping any of these, without and within ({ without: <condition>, deadline, keepers }: the inner condition did not hold by the deadline, or, for within, did, each dated by the named clock, blocks.md, A named clock). A condition of any other shape is data for its schema's readers: the protocol says nothing of it.
condition_ops_about: How a reading or a signal's amount keeps to a condition's value: less than, at most, greater than, at least, equal (promises.md, Conditions; profiles/tasks.md). Any other op holds for nothing.

repeat.rule: an RFC 5545 RRULE value, which may name another calendar by RFC 7529 RSCALE (RSCALE=HEBREW;FREQ=YEARLY); counted from state.when, in terms.zone (a calendar repeat with no zone is refused: the protocol fills in none)
repeat.keys_about: the keys of an event repeat { after, by, wait }: an occurrence each time an observe of kind `after` is written for this promise, by a signer `by` names (ids, or circle#role; with no `by` nothing starts one), due `wait` after the named clock's receipt of it, never after its own `at` (blocks.md, A named clock; a moon sighted, each batch); the occurrence is named by that observe's hash. The protocol checks the shape of a repeat; a reader works out its occurrences

terms_about: refrain: true makes a promise not to do something (no pesticide, sell only to me, never meat): it carries terms.until, moves nothing, and is breached only by a counted defeats of it by the deal's referee, or by its own signal condition holding at its until (folds.md); the side it was made to only disputes. Never done: once the reader's clock passes its until unbreached, the view says elapsed (decision H15). expires: ends an unanswered offer or ask; an ask may carry it or not (decision H11). condition: data under a schema; the protocol reads the condition_shapes, and a promise whose condition is { accepted: <first promise> } binds only once that deal binds (decision H17). zone: shaped like an IANA time zone name (Europe/London) that a repeat's dates are read in; read only beside a calendar repeat. pay_by: a time, when the price falls due; the fold reports it as due, beside paid_at, and judges no lateness. keepers: a named clock (blocks.md, A named clock) for the offer: an accept `needed` keepers received by `expires` is timely, and an event `when` or event repeat runs its wait from their receipt of the event; with none named there is no clock (no receipt dates anything). A schema the promise names may declare more terms (its state.terms): no fold reads them, so they bind no one.
narrower_than_about: A child grant's scope is narrower than its parent's on every field the parent states (authority.md): subset (every item is the parent's), subset-or-none (the same, a field left out naming none: `acts` and `parties`), at-most (an amount or money no larger, in the parent's unit or currency), at-least-duration (no shorter, counted from the parent's `at`), at-most-time (no later), superset (keeps every condition of the parent's). scope_refusals and limit_within_parent both read this table.
read_by_name_about: Ref keys and stop kinds a fold reads by name, not through a list in this file. A reader built without one is blind to it (tools/necessity.cjs).
